summary: Antigua's Citizenship by Investment Unit has published 19 six-monthly reports (2014 to H1 2024) with applications received by route and country, NDF contributions and passports issued by year. They give no approvals or denials, and their passports-by-year series changes between vintages. IMF Article IV reports (2014, 2022, 2023, 2025, 2026) and budget statements give CIP revenue to government (EC$60-158 million a year, 1-3% of GDP); vintages differ, notably for 2022 (EC$88.8m budget speech, 86 IMF prel., 68 later IMF). Program terms come from the 2013 Act/Regulations and amendments to 2024.

observations.quote: Tax revenue, non-tax revenue, and Citizen-by-Investment (CBI) revenue constituted 82.2, 8.4, and 9.4 percent of total revenue
observations.notes: Share of total revenue. Note: the table on p. 31 (62 of 926 total revenue and grants) would give about 6.7%; the basis of the 9.4% is not explained.

observations.quote: receipts from the Citizenship by Investment programme accounted for nearly 60 per cent of non-tax revenue and amounted to $88.8 million
observations.notes: Outturn stated in March 2023 budget speech. The 2024 budget speech says 2023's $67 million is 'the same level as in 2022', and the IMF's later tables give 68 for 2022; 88.8 is close to the IMF's preliminary 86 (Jan 2024 report).

observations.quote: this contribution is expected to amount to $67 million in 2023 - the same level as in 2022
observations.notes: Expected outturn given in Dec 2023. IMF later reports 62 for 2023.

observations.notes: Projected 2025 outturn in the Dec 2025 budget speech (the passage reviews 2025). IMF 2026 report: 158 (est.).

observations.quote: Non-tax revenue is expected to reach $240.7 million, including $120 million in CIP receipts and surpluses from state-owned enterprises.
observations.notes: Wording is ambiguous: '$120 million in CIP receipts and surpluses' may combine both items. The IMF projects 120 for CIP alone.

observations.quote: to date , about 150 new citizenships have been granted under the CIP
observations.notes: PM Gaston Browne to the Observer; period is from the June 2014 election to the article date. Approximate ('about').

observations.quote: about $50 million being pumped into the economy through the Citizenship by Investment Programme
observations.notes: Currency not stated (probably EC$ or US$); scope unclear. Same article gives the goal of 'about US $10 million a month'.

observations.quote: the programme has generated more than $1.4 billion in non-tax revenues for the people of Antigua and Barbuda
observations.notes: PM Gaston Browne, April 2026 ('$1.4 billion in 11 years'). IMI Daily gives it as EC$1.4 billion. Scale 'billion' as printed. Not reconcilable with the IMF/budget annual figures without the missing years.

observations.quote: the 2026 Budget projects EC$157 million (approximately US$58 million) in CIP revenue for the year

events.title: Citizenship by Investment Act 2013 published
events.description: Act No. 2 of 2013 (with the Regulations in its Schedule) was passed by the House on 1 Feb 2013 and the Senate on 19 Mar 2013, and published in the Gazette on 11 Apr 2013. The CIU started receiving applications later in 2013.
events.quote: Published in the Official Gazette Vol. XXXIII No. 20 dated 11th April, 2013.

events.title: Family NDF option at $540,000 (US$200,000) introduced
events.description: Amendment Regulations (S.I. 2013 No. 24) set the NDF contribution for a family of up to four at $540,000 and added a limited-time-offer regulation.
events.quote: the proposed contribution of the family to the National Development Fund shall be $540,000

events.title: Cabinet bars applicants from six countries
events.description: Cabinet restricted applications from nationals of Iran, Afghanistan, Iraq, North Korea, Somalia and Yemen, unless they are lawful permanent residents of Canada, the US or the UK.
events.quote: According to a decision by the Cabinet of Antigua and Barbuda, at its meeting held on Thursday, 11th December 2014, the Restricted Country List

events.title: Residence requirement cut to five days; names no longer laid before Parliament
events.description: August 2015 amendments cut the residence requirement from 35 days to 5 days in the first five years, offered a limited-time NDF cut from US$250,000 to US$200,000, reduced processing fees, and dropped the requirement to lay the names of economic citizens before Parliament every six months.
events.quote: the removal of the requirement that the names of economic citizens be brought to Parliament every six months

events.title: Canada requires visas from Antigua and Barbuda citizens
events.description: From 27 June 2017, Antigua and Barbuda citizens need a visitor visa for Canada; existing eTAs were cancelled.
events.quote: with effect from 5:30 am EDT on June 27, 2017, citizens of Antigua and Barbuda will need a visitor's visa

events.title: Observer reports discrepancies in CIU six-monthly reports
events.description: An Observer Media Group story (1 Jul 2017) alleged disparities between passport and application counts in the 2015 reports. The CIU replied that one application can cover several persons and gave figures by nationality (e.g. Iran: 27 applications, 33 passports).
events.quote: which subsequently emerged as Saturday's headline story, alleging disparities in the CIU's six-monthly reports

events.title: NDF threshold halved to US$100,000
events.description: Announced 12 Oct 2017; applications at US$100,000 (family of up to four) or US$125,000 (five or more) accepted from 1 Nov 2017. Legally a temporary offer to 31 Oct 2018 (S.I. 2017 No. 76), but it stayed in use until 31 Jul 2024.
events.quote: the Unit will be accepting Citizenship by Investment (CIP) applications under the new investment structure as of 1st November, 2017

events.title: Higher-education (UWI) investment route created
events.description: S.I. 2018 No. 16 added an investment route through contributions to designated higher-education institutions (later the UWI Fund; first applications appear in H2 2020).
events.quote: designate institutions of higher education where a person who desires to apply for Citizenship by Investment shall contribute not less than $150,000

events.title: Co-investment offer, foreign bank accounts and payment in any currency
events.description: S.I. 2019 No. 10 let two related parties invest $200,000 each in approved real estate until 31 Oct 2019, let the CIU open accounts outside the Eastern Caribbean, and allowed payment in any currency with Cabinet approval.
events.quote: the Unit may allow two related parties, with a minimum investment of $200,000 each

events.title: Oath of allegiance allowed by video link
events.description: S.I. 2020 No. 85 allowed the oath or affirmation of allegiance by Zoom, Skype or similar technology.
events.quote: allegiance or affirmation using zoom, skype or other similar audio-visual technology

events.title: CIU announces thresholds under five-country MoA, with 30-day delay
events.description: A CIU memo put into effect the Memorandum of Agreement among five OECS CBI states on a US$200,000 floor, but asked for 30 more days beyond the 30 June 2024 deadline to get Parliament's approval.
events.quote: executed between five heads of governments of OECS territories operating CIPs

events.title: New thresholds enacted: NDF US$230,000, real estate US$300,000, UWI US$260,000
events.description: S.I. 2024 No. 50 set the new US$ thresholds and a new fee schedule, and ended all limited-time offers at 11:59 p.m. on 31 Jul 2024.
events.quote: No applications based on a Limited Time Offer incentive offered by the Unit shall be accepted after the 31st July 2024 at 11:59 p.m.

events.title: US Proclamation restricts entry of Antigua and Barbuda nationals
events.description: The US Proclamation 'Restricting and Limiting the Entry of Foreign Nationals to Protect the Security of the United States' (16 Dec 2025) covered Antigua and Barbuda. The ambassador said visas already issued stay valid and new applications would face new biometric arrangements.
events.quote: following the issuance of the United States Proclamation entitled “Restricting and Limiting the Entry of Foreign Nationals to Protect the Security of the United States,” issued on 16 December 2025

events.title: Antigua and Barbuda included in US Visa Bond Pilot Program
events.description: Government statement confirms inclusion in the US visa-bond pilot for a narrow category of new visitor-visa applicants.
events.quote: while Antigua and Barbuda has been included in a U.S. Visa Bond Pilot Program

events.title: Regional CBI regulator agreement enacted into law
events.description: The IMF reports that an agreement setting up an independent regional regulator for CIPs has been enacted into law in Antigua and Barbuda and other ECCU CBI states (date of enactment not given; reported by May 2026).
events.quote: an agreement establishing an independent regulator for the industry has been enacted into law in Antigua and Barbuda

events.title: PM says EU could withdraw visa-free access by end of 2026
events.description: PM Browne said the EU had threatened to withdraw visa-free access, possibly by year end, and that the CIP would continue anyway.
events.quote: has threatened that they could withdraw their visa-free access potentially by the end of the year

programs.name: Antigua and Barbuda Citizenship by Investment Programme (CIP)
programs.notes: Set up by the Citizenship by Investment Act 2013 (gazetted 11 Apr 2013); run by the Citizenship by Investment Unit (CIU). Routes: National Development Fund donation, real estate, business investment, and (from 2018) University of the West Indies Fund. 5,203 applications from inception to 30 Jun 2024.

new_indicators.name: CBI passports issued
new_indicators.definition: Passports issued to people who got citizenship through the programme (main applicants and dependants) in a period, as reported by the programme unit
new_indicators.notes: Close to persons_naturalised but counts passports; Antigua's CIU reports it by year, and the yearly series changes between report vintages.

new_indicators.name: CBI fees collected by the programme unit
new_indicators.definition: Processing, due diligence, passport and agent licence fees collected by the CBI unit in a period, excluding donations and investments
new_indicators.notes: Antigua CIU operating account; not the same as cbi_fiscal_revenue.

new_indicators.name: CBI contributions collected
new_indicators.definition: Government contributions (donations) paid by applicants and collected by the programme agency in a period, excluding property purchases, investments and fees
new_indicators.notes: Same definition as proposed in the Malta inbox file. For Antigua: NDF contributions listed in CIU six-monthly reports.

gaps: No approval, denial or refusal counts found. The CIU six-monthly reports give only applications received (by country of birth and route), NDF contribution lists and passports issued; no report after H1 2024 is published on cip.gov.ag (checked the WordPress media and posts API on 28 Sep 2026).
Six-monthly reports for 2014 and H1 2015 exist only as a 2-page undated summary (atg-ciu-6m-2014); totals were not printed.
No IMF staff reports were published for Article IV consultations between 2015 and 2022 (only press releases); the 2016, 2018/2019 and 2021 consultations have no CIP revenue tables we could read.
No IMF or official series for total CBI inflows including real estate and business investment (only CIP revenue to government). The ECCB balance-of-payments data were not checked.

The Aug 2015 amendment (residency 35 to 5 days, NDF limited-time cut to US$200,000) and the 2015/2016 Citizenship by Investment (Amendment) Acts were not read in the original; only an Observer report reposted by the CIU was used.
No audited accounts of the NDF or CIU found, although the CIU web page says the NDF 'will also be audited by an internationally recognised accounting firm'.
The date the regional CBI regulator (ECCIRA) law was enacted in Antigua was not found in a primary source.
leads: Per-nationality application counts (Appendix I of each CIU report, 2014-H1 2024) could be extracted into a separate table; China is the largest source (834 of 2,420 applications to Dec 2019, 34.48%).

CIU operating-account disbursement lists (Cabinet-approved payments to carnival committees, Social Security, IMF loan payments, PV Energy escrow etc.) are in every report and could support a spending story.

IMF 2021 Article IV press release PR 21/246: https://www.imf.org/en/News/Articles/2021/08/12/pr21246-antigua-and-barbuda-imf-executive-board-concludes-2021-article-iv-consultation (may include a table with CIP revenue).
Budget statements for 2019-2022 and 2025 were not found at ab.gov.ag/pdf/budget/<year>/<year>_budget_statement.pdf; try other paths or the Parliament website.
Estimates of Revenue and Expenditure (ab.gov.ag) would give line-item CIP receipts, budgeted vs actual.
IMI Daily (2 Jul 2026) mentions a 'June 2028 phase-out date' from a Caribbean-EU meeting; check the EU Commission's visa suspension mechanism reports and the Saint Lucia government statement.
Antigua Observer original of the 1 Jul 2017 story on report discrepancies (antiguaobserver.com) - not located.
